# orca task

Every `orca task` command. Ids: a full id, a unique prefix, or (projects) a name or path.

## `orca task show <group> <task>`

one task of a group and its runs

- What it does: reads from the panel (no write).
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix

## `orca task retry <group> <task> [--agent <agent>] [--allow-observed-paths] [--work <work>]`

start again a task whose current run failed (the run read now is the one retried), optionally on another installation

- What it does: sends control verb `retry-task`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--agent <agent>`: retry on this agent installation instead (quota failover spec §8; not for a task with skills); `auto` hands the choice back to orca-auto (unlocks a task a switch pinned); refused to a run Orca dispatched
- `--allow-observed-paths`: allow only the exact paths the last blocked run reported missing; inspect `orca run show` first
- `--work <work>`: add work to the task's budget for this retry and every later run, as JSON {tokens?,activeMs?,attempts?,sessions?} (an omitted dimension adds 0); a person may always, an agent up to the orchestration agent top-up cap; refused to a run Orca dispatched; only a task under the optional token policy

## `orca task continue <group> <task> [--note <note>] [--note-scope <note-scope>]`

continue a task's current run from its newest complete checkpoint; --note tells its agent something

- What it does: sends control verb `continue-task`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--note <note>`: a note the continued run's agent reads at its next plan/execute (at most 4096 bytes)
- `--note-scope <note-scope>`: next-attempt (default) or remaining-attempts

## `orca task set-loop <group> <task> --file <file>`

set a task's loop plan from a JSON file {plan,inputs,work,workProvenance?,skills?}

- What it does: sends control verb `set-task-loop`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--file <file>` (required): the loop JSON

## `orca task set-labels <group> <task> [--label <label>] [--clear]`

set a task's labels (--label repeatable), or --clear back to the plan's

- What it does: sends control verb `set-task-labels`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--label <label>` (repeatable): a label
- `--clear`: drop the operator's labels

## `orca task verify-saved-result <group> <task> [--work <work>]`

verify the current run's saved result instead of re-running (after run eligibility says eligible)

- What it does: sends control verb `verify-saved-result`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--work <work>`: add work for the verification run as JSON {tokens?,activeMs?,attempts?,sessions?}; a person may always, an agent within the top-up cap; refused to a run Orca dispatched

## `orca task accept-attempt <group> <task> --run <run> --note <note>`

land a failed, settled run's last attempt after Orca re-runs the task's checks on it (an owner's act)

- What it does: sends control verb `accept-attempt`.
- Who may: a person: needs a person token over the socket (`orca auth login`, then `--as-person`).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--run <run>` (required): the terminal run whose last attempt to accept (orca run show <run> names it)
- `--note <note>` (required): why you accept it; recorded with the acceptance and in the run's decision ledger

## `orca task reopen <group> <task> --note <note>`

revoke a task's no-change completion and run it again in this group with a note for its agent

- What it does: sends control verb `reopen-task`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--note <note>` (required): what the agent should know; delivered as the new run's operator note (at most 2048 bytes)

## `orca task settle-usage <group> <task> --acknowledge <acknowledge>`

settle a run's unknown usage (cannot be undone)

- What it does: sends control verb `settle-unknown-usage`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `<task>`: a task id or a unique prefix
- `--acknowledge <acknowledge>` (required): charge-remaining-grant|charge-observed-floor|release-known-zero|release-unmetered: an agent may send charge-remaining-grant, or release-known-zero when ccloop proved the failed run spent nothing, or charge-observed-floor (charges only the floor ccloop observed, marked approximate; a finite remainder with a known floor, else refused observed-floor-unknown), without a person token; release-unmetered needs a person token (orca auth login, then --as-person); refused to a run Orca dispatched
